description: Building technology for the service of mankind.
summary:
Farm Sight is a web-based tool that will help farmers decide what crops to plant on their farm. It utilizes NASA satellite data to fill in 21 measurements that will affect plant growth, such as air quality, rain, heat, moisture, soil, and groundwater. Then through the user's inputted priorities (climate fit, soil health, and water savings), Farm Sight will calculate crop rotations using a world model of the field that simulates how it will respond to each crop across a simulated rotation. The app also shows how each rotation performs under current conditions and across every climate model in NASA's 2040 projections, including the worst years, helping farmers understand climate adaptation possibilities. Additionally, Farm Sight offers what-if forecasts for temperature and water availability, and a calculator for the years up until 2040. 
    Ultimately, Farm Sight offers farmers a easy to use tool that translates ambiguous NASA data into a clear plan with transparent explanations, while also keeping soil health and water usage in mind. Its machine learning is anchored to published standards. Therefore, it learns small, bounded corrections to those rules, which appear as a readable table an agronomist can check. This means that every recommendation is justified and verifiable, allowing farmers to make well-informed decisions for their farm.
details:
Farm Sight utilizes satellite imagery and climate data to propose sustainable crop rotations for farmers. Farmers will select their farm on our map and input their 3 priorities (climate adaptation, soil health, and water conservation), and the app ranks crop rotations by simulating each one with a world model of the field. Farm Sight will then provide them with ranked options for crop rotations, specific to their location. Each rotation will have an overall score, climate-fit score, soil health assessment, water savings estimate, and performance given 2040 climate projections.

Farm Sight is beneficial because it takes hours of manual data gather and turns it into one click on the map by using NASA data and other reliable sources. Farm Sight also explains each recommendation backed up with reliable information and world models. In addition, our project also has prediction capabilities into the future that will show how different rotations will perform into the future.

We used Python as our coding language and pulled data from NASA POWER, GRACE-FO, SRTM, NEX-GDDP-CMIP6, ISRIC SoilGrids, and USDA Cropland Data Layer. Our website is hosted on Streamlit which allows it to have backend functionality that is seamlessly integrated into our frontend design. Imagery is implemented into Farm Sight with NASA and IBM's Prithvi-EO-2.0 foundation model, where the world model learns how a field develops over time using ten years of crop maps, 16-day greenness and weather data.

Our project is creative because it translates satellite data that is available to everyone into useful, actionable data for farmers. Unlike existing satellite world models, which only forecast how vegetation responds to weather, ours model treats the farmer's crop choice as an action, so entire rotations can be simulated and compared. Furthermore, our model is neurosymbolic. Rather than a black box, our model's machine learning is confined to small, bounded corrections to published agronomic standards, which come out as a revised rule table, ultimately taking years of data and experience and turns it into ranked choices and explanations for farmers understand and implement with ease.

Some key considerations that our team had to consider was what would happen to our world model architecture if data for a location did not exist and ultimately decided that missing data would stay visible, without any guessing or prediction. We prioritized transparency by showing the rule-based reasoning and any learned rule corrections behind each score, rather than hiding recommendations inside a model.
